title: Spring Service Calls and Kafka Messaging: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on calling other services with RestClient, WebClient and declarative HTTP interfaces, with timeouts and error handling, then Spring Kafka producers, @KafkaListener consumers, retries and dead-letter topics.

chapters.title: HTTP Clients: The Mental Model
points: RestClient (Spring 6.1+) is the synchronous, fluent client that replaces RestTemplate for new code; build it with RestClient.builder().baseUrl(...).build() or inject the auto-configured RestClient.Builder
WebClient is the reactive, non-blocking client from spring-webflux: it returns Mono/Flux and nothing is sent until you subscribe, with .block() as the escape hatch to wait for the result
Comparison: RestClient blocks a thread and suits MVC and virtual threads; WebClient suits streaming and high fan-out calls; RestTemplate is in maintenance mode, so avoid it in new code
Always build clients from the injected Builder, not a bare new, so Boot's message converters, observability and customizers apply
Mistake: calling block() inside a reactive pipeline, or building a new client per request, which throws away the connection pool

chapters.title: Making Calls and Declarative HTTP Interfaces
points: RestClient call chain: client.get().uri("/users/{id}", id).retrieve().body(User.class), and use body(new ParameterizedTypeReference<List<User>>(){}) for generics
POST with a body: client.post().uri("/users").contentType(APPLICATION_JSON).body(dto).retrieve().toBodilessEntity(), and use toEntity(User.class) when you need status or headers
WebClient equivalent: webClient.get().uri("/users/{id}", id).retrieve().bodyToMono(User.class), and bodyToFlux(User.class) for streams
Declarative interface: annotate an interface with @HttpExchange("/users") and methods with @GetExchange("/{id}") or @PostExchange, taking @PathVariable, @RequestParam and @RequestBody

Create the proxy with HttpServiceProxyFactory.builderFor(RestClientAdapter.create(restClient)).build().createClient(UserApi.class), exposed as a @Bean; the adapter can instead wrap a WebClient. Mistake: forgetting that a missing adapter or registration yields no bean, and that the interface is only a proxy

chapters.title: Timeouts and Error Handling for Outbound Calls
points: Defaults are effectively unbounded, so always set a connect timeout and a read timeout; a missing timeout lets one slow dependency exhaust your thread pool

RestClient timeouts: set them on the request factory, for example JdkClientHttpRequestFactory with HttpClient.newBuilder().connectTimeout(...) plus setReadTimeout(...), or use Boot's spring.http.client.connect-timeout and read-timeout properties

WebClient timeouts: Reactor Netty HttpClient.create().option(CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MILLIS, 2000).responseTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(3)), wrapped in ReactorClientHttpConnector; a per-call .timeout(Duration) on the Mono also works

retrieve() throws on 4xx and 5xx: RestClient raises HttpClientErrorException and HttpServerErrorException (both RestClientResponseException), WebClient raises WebClientResponseException; customize with .onStatus(HttpStatusCode::is4xxClientError, (req, res) -> { throw new MyException(res.getStatusCode()); })

Mistake: retrying non-idempotent POSTs blindly, or catching the generic Exception and hiding the status; with WebClient use retryWhen(Retry.backoff(3, Duration.ofMillis(200))) only for idempotent calls and transient errors

chapters.title: Kafka Producers and @KafkaListener Consumers
points: Producer: inject KafkaTemplate<String,Order> and call send(topic, key, value), which returns a CompletableFuture<SendResult> (not blocking); attach whenComplete to log failures
The record key decides the partition, so the same key always lands on the same partition and keeps per-key ordering; a null key spreads records across partitions with no ordering guarantee

Reliability settings: acks=all plus enable.idempotence=true avoid loss and duplicates on producer retry; configure spring.kafka.producer.key-serializer and value-serializer (JsonSerializer for objects)

Consumer: @KafkaListener(topics="orders", groupId="billing") on a method; consumers in one group split the partitions between them, different groups each get every record, and concurrency cannot usefully exceed the partition count

Offset handling: the default AckMode.BATCH commits after the poll batch is processed; use MANUAL with Acknowledgment.acknowledge() for control, and set auto.offset.reset=earliest for a new group. Mistake: a slow listener exceeds max.poll.interval.ms and triggers a rebalance, and the value deserializer trusts packages only if spring.json.trusted.packages is set

chapters.title: Retries and Dead-Letter Topics
points: By default a listener exception triggers DefaultErrorHandler, which retries in place 10 times with no delay and then logs and skips the record; override with a DefaultErrorHandler bean using new FixedBackOff(1000L, 3) or ExponentialBackOff

Dead-letter topic: new DefaultErrorHandler(new DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer(kafkaTemplate), backOff) publishes the failed record to <topic>.DLT on the same partition, with the exception details in headers

Non-retryable exceptions such as deserialization or validation errors should skip retries via addNotRetryableExceptions(...); wrap the deserializer in ErrorHandlingDeserializer so a poison message goes to the DLT rather than looping forever

Non-blocking retries: @RetryableTopic(attempts="4", backoff=@Backoff(delay=1000, multiplier=2)) creates retry topics (orders-retry-0, orders-retry-1 ...) plus orders-dlt, and a @DltHandler method consumes the dead letters; unlike blocking retries it does not stall the partition, but it breaks ordering
Mistakes: retrying forever on a permanent failure, making listeners non-idempotent (delivery is at-least-once so duplicates happen), and never monitoring or replaying the DLT

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Clients and Kafka
points: Clients: RestClient (sync) for MVC, WebClient (reactive) for streaming, @HttpExchange interface plus HttpServiceProxyFactory for typed proxies; always build from the injected Builder
Call shape: .get().uri(...).retrieve().body(T.class) for RestClient and .bodyToMono(T.class) for WebClient; retrieve() throws on 4xx and 5xx, handle with onStatus
Timeouts: set connect and read timeouts on every client, since the default is unbounded; retry only idempotent calls with backoff
Kafka send: kafkaTemplate.send(topic, key, value) returns a future; the key picks the partition and so decides ordering; use acks=all with idempotence enabled
Consume: @KafkaListener(topics, groupId); same group shares partitions, different groups each get all records; concurrency is capped by partition count

Errors: DefaultErrorHandler with a BackOff and DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer sends to <topic>.DLT; use ErrorHandlingDeserializer for bad payloads and @RetryableTopic for non-blocking retries; keep consumers idempotent
